A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preservation of the dinosaur eggs in the Seonso Conglometer at Boseong was facilitated by calcareous pedagenesis and semiarid climate.
the dinosaur egg-bearing deposits of Boseong are interpreted to have been laid and incubated on a floodplain, and the eggs were preserved in palaeosols that formed on the floodplain.
